frontier.observed: ClayVerse performs incomplete-episode recovery, ClayGraph rebuild, boot checkpointing, Clerk/Claude/EntityOS validation and durable terminal/tmux setup before uvicorn.run starts the HTTP listener. The current Kata profile had readiness and liveness probes but no startupProbe.
frontier.hypothesis: A legitimate slow boot/recovery can fail /healthz before the HTTP listener exists and be killed by liveness before startup completes, producing restart churn and confusing Tier-1/Tier-2 recovery evidence.
frontier.counterhypothesis: All accepted startup/recovery paths always complete before the liveness failure window, making a startup probe unnecessary.
frontier.cheapest_discriminator: Add a finite startupProbe on the existing narrow /healthz surface and later inject a controlled slow startup below/above the admitted budget in an authorized Kubernetes/Kata execution.

primary_upstream_basis: Kubernetes official probe documentation: when a startupProbe is configured, liveness and readiness do not run until startup succeeds; startup failure remains bounded by failureThreshold times periodSeconds.
promotion_gate: In an authorized isolated Kubernetes/Kata-capable run, prove a deliberately delayed but valid startup inside the 300-second budget is not restarted, prove an intentionally hung startup exceeding the budget is terminated, and then continue exact-image Tier-2/recovery acceptance.

unusual_experiment.reason: No safely shared immutable request/turn identity is exposed for the global GO experiment lease.
